newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK GOVERNOR PREPARES TO STEP DOWN.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK GOVERNOR PREPARES TO STEP DOWN.

text.p: Bulgarian National Bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Friday he was prepared to step down once parliament decided whom to appoint as his successor to run the bank under a currency board system.

"I told the speaker of the parliament that I am prepared to resign from the BNB, when the politicians appoint a new BNB governor who will rule the bank in the conditions of the new BNB law," Filipov told reporters.
Filipov met parliament's speaker Yordan Sokolov to hand in the 1996 BNB report.

Under a $657 million reform and funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund, Bulgaria pledged to introduce a restrictive monetary regime known as a currency board to restore confidence in the volatile national currency.

Under the system, due to be introduced in mid-year, the central bank would be banned from lending to the government and commercial banks. The amount of levs in circulation should be matched exactly by the amount of foreign exchange reserves.
"It would be unrealistic to restructure the BNB now without giving a say to the person who will have to govern it," said Filipov.

Bulgaria's parliament has yet to pass amendments to the BNB act, which would restructure the central bank into an issue department, bank supervision department and banking department, to be used as lender of last resort only if systemic risk occurs.
Parliament is also due to appoint a new BNB governor and management to operate the bank in a currency board system later this month.

Filipov, was the head of lev operations department and BNB board member for several years before succeeding Todor Valchev as governor in January 1996. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
